The Prophet held a horse race, trained horses running from Al-Hafya' to Thaniyat Al-Wada' and untrained ones from there to the mosque of Bani Zuraiq, with Ibn Umar taking part.
Horses bring reward to one keeping them for Allah's cause, shelter to one earning by them, and sin to one keeping them for pride; donkeys fall under the atom's-weight verse.
When Medina was alarmed, the Prophet borrowed Abu Talha's horse Al-Mandub, rode out, found nothing to fear, and praised the horse's speed.
Good remains in horses' foreheads till Resurrection, bringing reward or booty; a horse kept for Allah's cause earns reward for its feed and dung; horses named al-Jarada and al-Luhaif appear.
When Medina took fright, the Prophet borrowed a horse called Mandub, rode out, found nothing to fear, and said the horse was very fast.
Horses bring reward, shelter or sin; the Prophet speeds Jabir's tired camel and buys it, finds Mandub fast, and gives a horse two booty shares, its rider one.
The Prophet rode an unsaddled horse, sword slung on, Abu Talha's slow horse became unbeatable, he arranged horse races over set courses, and his she-camel al-Adba was once outrun.
The Prophet urges Bani Aslam to practise archery, as their father Ishmael was an archer, and at Badr orders arrows shot when the enemy comes near.
The Prophet shares Abu Talha's shield, and Fatima stops his bleeding when his helmet is smashed; Bani an-Nadir's fai buys arms and horses; Sa'd is urged to shoot.
The Prophet rides with a sword at his neck; conquerors' swords bore no gold or silver; a bedouin who seized his sword is spared; Abu Qatada spears an onager.
When Medina was alarmed the Prophet rode Abu Talha's horse out alone, found nothing to fear, and said the horse, once slow, was very fast.
Flag-bearer Qais bin Sa'd combs his hair for Hajj; at Khaibar the flag goes to Ali, who came despite eye trouble; Az-Zubair is told where to fix the flag.
Finding men of Aslam at archery, the Prophet urges the offspring of Ishmael to shoot, as their father was an archer, and says he is with both teams.
Passing men of Aslam at archery, the Prophet told the children of Ishmael to shoot, their father being an archer, and said he was with both teams.
Blessed by the Prophet, Urwa profited in every deal; goodness is in horses until the Resurrection, a horse bringing reward, a living or sin according to why it is kept.
When fear spread in Medina, the Prophet rode Abu Talha's horse and said they saw nothing, but found the horse like a sea.

Horses bring reward if kept for Allah's Cause, shelter if kept for a living, and sin if kept for pride; for donkeys the Prophet cited only the atom's-weight verse.
